To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inflation targeting policies, which are based on a pegged float exchange rate, have the potential of increasing the nominal exchange rate and, in the same time, of decreasing the consumer price index.
• The Romanian economy is more vulnerable to the exchange rate shocks than the other countries from Central Europe (CE).

(a) an increase in the coefficient of the Central Bank’s interventions on the forex currency markets leads to a reduction of the inflation rate, to a deterioration of the real economic growth and the foreign trade balance and to an appreciation of the nominal exchange rate; (b) an increase in Central Bank’s interventions in the monetary markets leads to an increase in the inflation rate, a reduction of the real economic and the foreign trade balances and to a depreciation of the nominal exchange rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: • What is the effect of the CBE and CBM coefficients on the inflation and on the nominal exchange rate, respectively?

the effects on the real economic growth of the changes in the Central Bank’s interventions on the domestic monetary and forex markets, and with the effects on inflation and exchange rate of the changes in CBE and CBM.

the following questions: • what are the effects of the Central Bank’s interventions on the exchange rate and the interest rate? • what are the implications of the exchange rate and interest rate on the economic activity? • what are effects on the consumer price index? • what are implications for the foreign trade balance?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Romanian economy is not yet mature enough to be able to implement the inflation targeting policy.
the “exchange rate policy” has a strong impact on “inflation targeting”, and vice versa.

the Romanian monetary authorities should not pursue a policy of pegged floating of the national currency, because this policy would have negative implications in terms of the real economic growth and inflation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “inflation targeting policies”, as a whole, are not compatible with the pegged float exchange rate system.
, in the case of a pegged exchange rate regime, an inflation targeting policy would be an efficient tool for the Central Bank to pursue its objectives of price stability and economic growth.
the exchange rate policy is the most important determinant of the Romanian inflation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of a pegged exchange rate regime, the Central Bank’s monetary policy can be effective only if the CBE coefficient is sufficiently low.
the exchange rate pegging regime has to be supported by the Central Bank’s interventions on the forex market.

the exchange rate policy is the most effective tool for the Central Bank to achieve its inflation target, and the exchange rate policy can be implemented without significant effects on the real economic growth and the trade balance.
